## Another Day, Another Dominant Performance

You know, I've been around this game long enough to recognize when a model's got its rhythm, and folks, we're in one of those stretches. Twelve wins against three losses on September 12th—that's the kind of day that reminds me why I still love doing this after all these years.

The 80% hit rate isn't just a number on a spreadsheet. It's the result of seeing patterns others miss, understanding how September baseball operates differently, and respecting the fundamentals that never change.

## Breaking Down Yesterday's Action

The Tigers delivered for us again—that makes it two days in a row we've liked Detroit, and two days in a row they've come through. When you see a team trending like that in September, you take notice.

The Rays pulled through in a tight one against Houston, the Sox handled Kansas City, and the Padres took care of business in San Francisco. These weren't flukes. These were calculated predictions based on matchup advantages and situational baseball.

## The Misses: Yankees and Dodgers

Let's talk about the two that got away. The Yankees couldn't handle the Mets in the Subway Series—that's baseball in September for you. Rivalry games have their own logic, and sometimes the underdog just wants it more.

The Dodgers falling to Miami? I've seen this movie before. Late-season games in Florida can be tricky, especially when a team's already thinking about October. No excuses, just reality.

## Looking Ahead to September 13

Now, about tomorrow. We're going back to the well with Detroit, and I'll tell you why I'm comfortable with that decision.

## Why Detroit Again?

Jackson Jobe on the mound for Detroit, Gabriel Hughes for Colorado. When you've got the Rockies traveling—especially this late in the season—you're looking at a team that's ready for the offseason. The Tigers, meanwhile, are playing meaningful baseball.

I've covered enough September games to know that momentum and motivation matter as much as talent. Detroit's got both right now. At 69% confidence, this is the kind of edge you don't pass up.

The model's been hot, Detroit's been reliable, and the matchup favors the home team. Sometimes it really is that straightforward.

**See you after first pitch tomorrow.**

— Max
